HKU_CH105.title: HKU Stephen Hui Geological Museum: Plants in the dinosaur world, Ginkgo yimaensis CH105
HKU_CH105.note: Primary museum specimen record. Label Ginkgo yimaensis Zhou et Zhang, Middle Jurassic China, displayed size13cm. Original defining paper not acquired. Photograph shows one long petiole and deeply divided lobed lamina, not a branch or modern biloba fan. Specimen-based organ interpretation, not an exact cast.
HKU_CH105.inspection: Personally inspected museum full page and original CH105 photograph before concept; six conspicuous elongate lobes/fan divisions and a long single petiole, no evidence of short shoot.

VANDERPAS2017.title: Van Der Pas, Poppe and Van Waveren2017: Ontogenetic variability in old and new collections of Dicranophyllum gallicum
VANDERPAS2017.note: Primary full text and figures6,12. Narrow leaves commonly twice bifurcate; second fork wider. Helical leaf cushions and foliage distributed along slender axis, denser apex. Whole height4.5m is a mechanical woody reconstruction assumption, not fossil completeness; this smaller illustrative living specimen uses1.6m nominal axis. No roots or reproduction claimed.
VANDERPAS2017.inspection: Personally inspected original fossil Fig6 and original author reconstruction Fig12, plus complete relevant morphology and reconstruction text. License CC BY4.0, used consult-only without copying pixels.

SIMUNEK_BEK2003.title: Simunek and Bek2003: Noeggerathiaceae from the Carboniferous basins of the Bohemian Massif
SIMUNEK_BEK2003.note: Primary full paper text read through publicly indexed author-uploaded ResearchGate version. Original inventory2015 Elsevier item unavailable and replaced transparently. Direct2003 PDF download403; original2003 detailed margin plate pixels NOT obtained. Text supports obovate-obcuneate pinnules, shallow dentate or lobed distal edges and fan dichotomous venation; small basal pairs and narrowing apex. Full frond50-60cm is authors reconstruction. Actual holotype plate supplied by National Museum2021 source below. No cuticle anatomy modeled.
SIMUNEK_BEK2003.inspection: Author Fig11 whole reconstruction personally viewed via attributed teaching-page reproduction; it supports overall frond arrangement only, NOT fine leaf-end details. Fine teeth follow primary text, with holotype pixel resolution limitation explicitly retained.

NM2021_E122A.title: Kvacek, Daskova and Libertin2021: Catalogue of Plant Fossils Described in Works by Kaspar M. Sternberg, Second Revised Edition
NM2021_E122A.note: Primary museum catalogue, printedp102 and Plate22 printedp260, NM-E122a holotype Noeggerathia foliosa. Original fossil photo inspected. It confirms broad attached wedge-obovate pinnules and tapering rachis; fine marginal denticles are not reliably resolved in this photograph, so conservative shallow dentition follows2003 text rather than claimed measured holotype teeth. Other species on plate explicitly excluded.
NM2021_E122A.inspection: Actual official PDF page262 rendered and personally viewed at2100px before Noeggerathia concept. Fig1 only is N.foliosa. Fig2-5 are not evidence for this model.

HARRIS1961.title: T. M. Harris1961: The Fossil Cycads
HARRIS1961.note: Original article downloaded and scanned pages personally read with OCR assistance. Bjuvia simplex leaf and Palaeocycas integer reproductive organ association is circumstantial, no organic attachment. This candidate is ONLY a Bjuvia simplex leaf organ, not Florin whole-plant hypothesis. No leaf rosette, trunk, reproductive organ or precise fullplant claim.
HARRIS1961.inspection: Original scans pp314-316 personally inspected/read before concept. Modern material or wholeplant render is not fossil evidence.

BARBACKA2021.title: Barbacka and Bodor2021: A valodi Jurassic Park, Studia Comloensis1(1), Fig11
BARBACKA2021.note: Primary institutional authors fossil photograph credited Barbacka Maria, Bjuvia simplex, printedp8 Fig11. Strong midrib and densely transverse open parallel veins in broad undivided leaf; incomplete specimen does not certify complete outline. Jurassic specimen is comparative morphology, not claimed identical to Harris Triassic association. Adjacent wholeplant painting not used as factual reconstruction.
BARBACKA2021.inspection: Actual photograph personally inspected before concept; original institutional caption read. Consult-only copyrighted image, retained in prior raw source location without copying into Git.

KOVACS1976.title: Kovacs-Endrody1976: Glossopteris from Hammanskraal, original browniana specimen comparison
KOVACS1976.note: Primary source pp71-72 PlateIVe, specimen H.I.15. Actual Glossopteris browniana reference demonstrates a midrib/bundle and anastomosing polygonal vein mesh, unlike Bjuvia open near-transverse parallel veins. Only a comparison, never substitute subject. Original84 model hashes pinned separately; no prior rendered pixels become97 evidence.
KOVACS1976.inspection: Primary text and actual PlateIV photograph personally read/viewed. Shape alone overlaps and cannot establish distinction. Distinct venation connectivity must remain evident in new neutral geometry comparison.
